The given operator is a third-order differential operator of the form

$$
D(y)={a}_{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}+{a}_{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{a}_{1}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{a}_{0}y
$$

with constant coefficients  ${a}_{3}=1,{a}_{2}=-3,{a}_{1}=4,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

To compute $D(y),$ we apply the definition of the operator $D$ to the function $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}D(y) & =D(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =(\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-3\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x})(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-3\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-3(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$
